key_insight: APOE allele effects vary across ancestry and sex, with 27 phenotype associations and proteomic signals suggesting both shared and population-specific biology.
clinical_relevance: These findings support ancestry-aware interpretation of APOE-based risk, especially for dementia and liver-related phenotypes, and point to candidate biomarkers such as SNAP25 for future validation.
method: Phenome-wide association study in 367,757 All of Us participants across six genetic ancestry groups
Tested APOE genotypes against 2,632 phenotypes using an Alzheimer’s-disease-risk ordinal hierarchy
Analyzed plasma proteomics in 9,132 participants across five ancestries, including sex- and ancestry-stratified heterogeneity tests
evidence_signal: The analysis found 27 APOE-associated phenotypes, 5 sex-heterogeneous lipid traits, 9 ancestry-specific associations, and proteomic links including SNAP25 across ancestries.
watch_item: Results are observational and depend on EHR-derived phenotypes, so ancestry-specific findings and biomarker candidates need replication and functional validation before translation.
paper_title: Phenome-wide and proteomic analysis of APOE alleles across different ancestries in the All of Us Research Program
